Senses.Explanation: Kashyapa is the figure whom the Chan record places at the first public handover. At the Vulture Peak assembly, the World-Honored One holds up a flower before the silent gathering; Kashyapa alone breaks into a smile, after which the Buddha says that he entrusts the treasury of the true eye of the teaching to Mahakashyapa. Later Chan records do not leave him inside a biography: they repeatedly raise, question, and comment on this scene. Yuelin says that when the World-Honored One held up the flower and Kashyapa smiled, both deserved thirty blows. Kashyapa also appears at the teaching seat: after the assembly gathers, he strikes the sounding block and announces, “the World-Honored One has finished speaking the teaching,” and the Buddha leaves the seat. In the succession encounter with Ananda, Ananda asks what was transmitted besides the gold-thread robe; Kashyapa calls “Ananda,” receives his answer, and says, “knock down the flagpole before the gate.” These public acts—smile and announced entrustment, closing the Buddha's assembly, and the robe-and-flagpole exchange with Ananda—are Kashyapa's defining Chan deployment.
Senses.Note: This sense is Mahakashyapa, identifiable in the cited Chan cases by the flower, the entrusted eye-treasury, Ananda, or the gold-thread robe. The earlier Kashyapa Buddha is a different figure and is recorded separately below by his Zen deployment.

Occurrences.AttributionNote: The Patriarchs' Hall Collection (祖堂集), Guifeng Zongmi section, Reply to the Ten Questions of Layman Shi. Shi Zhicheng is the exact questioner: the reference to entrusting the teaching to Mahakasyapa occurs in his ninth question; Guifeng Zongmi is the respondent.

Senses.Explanation: The same name also identifies Kashyapa Buddha, the earlier buddha invoked at the opening of Baizhang's wild-fox case. The old man says that in Kashyapa Buddha's time he lived on that mountain, answered that a person of great cultivation does not fall into cause and effect, and consequently fell into a wild-fox body for five hundred lives. Chan texts deploy this earlier Buddha as the time-marker that makes the old man's former teaching office and karmic consequence intelligible; this is a different figure from Mahakashyapa of the flower, robe, and Ananda cases.
Senses.Note: Three allowlisted records anchor the exact phrase “in the time of the former Kashyapa Buddha” (過去迦葉佛時) in the public wild-fox case. The definition stays with that Zen deployment and does not import an external buddha biography.
